title: Private onramp & egress constraints - AetherWave intake
next_steps: Redwood to share SOC 2 & ISO whitepaper and KMS/HSM security notes
SE to run a small latency/egress benchmark on AetherWave sample traces (target next week)
Schedule canary pilot planning call w/ transit gateway diagram (tentative 2027-06-15)
Send initial pricing estimate for Dedicated + Private onramp
action_items: Rohit: prepare architecture sketch showing private endpoints + transit gateway options (due 2027-06-11)
Maya: send security pack (SOC2, pen test, audit logs) and SSO integration guide (due 2027-06-09)
Liam: share egress volume spreadsheet and list of regions required (due 2027-06-10)
Sara: compile compliance checklist for data residency & encryption used in pilot (due 2027-06-12)
meeting_header:
Date: 2027-06-08
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Rohit Patel (Redwood SE), Evelyn Park (Redwood CSM); Liam O'Neal, Sara Nguyen, Tomás Rivera, Nisha Kapoor (AetherWave)
summary: Discovery focused on Private/VPC onramp options. AetherWave has strict egress/residency constraints and prefers private endpoints or transit gateway peering. Discussed Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs, KMS, SSO, and pilot steps. Action items agreed to share security materials and run benchmarks.
topics: Transit gateway and Direct Connect options
Security: SOC2, KMS/HSM, SSO/SAML, audit logs
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: okay everyone thanks for joining i think we have about 50 minutes so we'll try to cover networking constraints, security and next steps. um quick roll call?
[00:12] Liam O'Neal: Liam here, head of infra at AetherWave. hey Maya.
[00:15] Sara Nguyen: Sara - security architect.
[00:17] Tomás Rivera: Tomas - SRE.
[00:20] Nisha Kapoor: Nisha - PM.
[00:22] Maya Chen: great thanks. Rohit and Evelyn from our side?
[00:25] Rohit Patel: Rohit here. i'll jump into the technical bits.
[00:27] Evelyn Park: Evelyn - i'll be helping coordinate follow ups.
[00:30] Maya Chen: perfect. quick context: AetherWave told us they want private deployment for regulated telemetry ingestion and model inference inside their VPCs, low egress footprint to public net, and strict region gating - is that correct Liam?
[00:44] Liam O'Neal: yeah that's right. we have european and apac customers where data residency is a hard requirement. also our compliance team is picky about external egress; they want audit logs and KMS integration.
[00:55] Sara Nguyen: to add, we need SAML SSO and RBAC integration up front and we can't allow model weights to leave our environment unencrypted.
[01:05] Maya Chen: absolutely makes sense. so there are a couple options with Redwood: hosted, dedicated reserved capacity, or private (VPC/private control plane). for your constraints we're focusing on Private deployment — that gives you a private control plane and can be deployed in your VPC or via a VPC peering/transit gateway model.
[01:30] Tomás Rivera: quick question on wording — what's the difference between private endpoints and VPC peering in your setup?
[01:36] Rohit Patel: good question. so private endpoints (like privatelink-style) let you expose an endpoint in your VPC and traffic stays on the cloud provider backbone to our infra. VPC peering or transit gateway would actually peer your VPCs into a Redwood-managed VPC or we can deploy the inference nodes into your account if you prefer. each has tradeoffs for egress and routing.
[01:56] Nisha Kapoor: and do you support direct connect or expressroute? some of our onprem sites route via direct connect and we want low egress hops.
[02:05] Rohit Patel: yes we can integrate with Direct Connect/ExpressRoute. typically the architecture is either: 1) Redwood nodes run in your account (on-prem-equivalent private deployment) or 2) we run in our account and peer via transit gateway / privatelink. if you use direct connect, traffic doesn't traverse the public internet.
[02:22] Liam O'Neal: curious about egress charging - if traffic stays on the provider backbone do we still get egress fees?
[02:28] Maya Chen: good point. egress can still apply depending on the cloud provider bookkeeping; peering within the same region is usually cheaper, cross-region or cross-AZ transfers may have costs. in our pricing for Private we model expected egress and can include a billing line item in Dedicated contracts. but we need your expected outbound volumes to estimate.
[02:47] Sara Nguyen: we'll share a spreadsheet of token and payload volumes. one more security ask: can you support customer-managed KMS for model keys? we must retain control of key material.
[02:58] Rohit Patel: yes we support customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations; you'll see options in the security pack. the runtime can be configured to encrypt KV cache and model artifacts at rest with your KMS. small caveat: for some quantized model variant uploads we need a transfer step but it's encrypted and can be done over your private link.
[03:20] Tomás Rivera: you mentioned runtime and KV cache — does Redwood keep any cached tokens outside our VPC?
[03:26] Rohit Patel: in Private mode no; we can keep KV cache within your VPC or in a customer-owned subnet. in Hosted mode caches are in Redwood infra. but for your use we would design so cached state doesn't leave your boundary.
[03:36] Nisha Kapoor: timeline wise we're trying to get pilot running in Q3 — is that realistic?
[03:41] Maya Chen: yes Q3 pilot seems doable. typical pilot is 4-6 weeks: onboarding and network setup (1-2 weeks), initial E2E benchmarks (1 week), then an internal pilot and validation (2-3 weeks).
[03:55] Liam O'Neal: what about canary rollouts and fallback? if a node goes down we need graceful degradation to a cheaper hosted endpoint?
[04:03] Rohit Patel: we offer routing policies - you can route by latency, cost, or tier. canary and automatic fallbacks are supported in the control plane. if you want to fallback to hosted, we can encrypt payloads and route to a hosted variant but that requires compliance sign-off.
[04:19] Sara Nguyen: fallback to hosted probably won't pass our compliance unless we do data tokenization. can you do tokenization or pseudonymization at ingress?
[04:26] Rohit Patel: yes we have pre-processing hooks that can tokenize or strip PII before hitting the model. that's part of the pipeline we can turn on.
[04:34] Maya Chen: just to flag, we'll include the data flow diagram in the security packet so your team can see where tokenization happens.
[04:41] Nisha Kapoor: region gating — we need the inference to run only in eu-west-1 and ap-southeast-2 for a subset of customers and block anything else. is that supported?
[04:52] Rohit Patel: absolutely. deployments can be pinned to region(s) and we can enforce routing that prevents serving from other regions. we also support geo-fencing rules at the edge and in the control plane.
[05:03] Liam O'Neal: what about model weights — if you run the model in your account or our account do the weights ever transfer back to Redwood?
[05:10] Rohit Patel: if we deploy nodes into your account, weights live in your storage and never leave. if we host them in Redwood account for convenience, we can still ensure encryption and key ownership via your KMS but the copies will be in Redwood-controlled storage. we can do either based on your compliance appetite.
[05:25] Tomás Rivera: any lock-in concerns if we start with privatelink and later want to manage inference ourselves?
[05:31] Maya Chen: good question. our deployments are versioned and you can export model artifacts and configs; the goal is to avoid lock-in. we'll provide migration docs and a model export path.
[05:41] Nisha Kapoor: okay can we talk about network topology options — peering vs privatelink vs deploying nodes in our account? pros/cons?
[05:49] Rohit Patel: sure. privatelink: easy to set up, low management overhead, traffic goes over cloud backbone, good for smaller egress. peering/transit gateway: better for high-throughput and less NATing, easier for direct connect onprem routing. deploying nodes in your account: best for strict compliance, gives you full control but requires more ops on your side.
[06:10] Sara Nguyen: do you have any documented ip ranges/ASN lists for firewall allow-listing?
[06:15] Maya Chen: yes we'll send a CIDR and ASN list for the nodes and endpoints. for private deployments deployed in your account, obviously you'll control the subnets.
[06:24] Liam O'Neal: when you say "send" do you mean publicly? our security team wants a signed artifact.
[06:29] Evelyn Park: we'll attach the network diagram and an official allow-list PDF in the follow-up email; it's part of the security pack.
[06:36] Tomás Rivera: how do you handle NAT egress from our subnets if we host in our account? we have strict egress e2e monitoring.
[06:44] Rohit Patel: if nodes are in your account, egress is under your control — we can avoid NAT by using private subnets and route tables. if you need dedicated egress IPs, we support NAT gateways or egress via a set of managed appliances we can provision.
[06:58] Nisha Kapoor: sorry to jump back — what's the expected devops effort from our side for a private deployment in our account?
[07:05] Rohit Patel: you'll need basic infra: VPCs, subnets, security groups, IAM roles, and optionally Direct Connect. Redwood provides terraform modules and a deployment script; typical onboarding requires one infra engineer for 2-3 days of work plus coordination for KMS and SSO.
[07:22] Liam O'Neal: terraform modules sound good. do we need to open tickets for support during pilot?
[07:27] Maya Chen: you'll get a dedicated CSM and we provide SE support during onboarding. for Dedicated/Private enterprise contracts we also offer a technical account manager for escalations.
[07:37] Sara Nguyen: audit logs — we need to retain request-level logs for 12 months for compliance. is that supported?
[07:42] Rohit Patel: yes request-level audit logs can be forwarded to your logging bucket or SIEM; retention policies are configurable. we can also provide token-level cost breakdowns if needed.
[07:54] Nisha Kapoor: about the pilot — what does success look like for Redwood and for us?
[07:59] Maya Chen: good to document. for you: low-latency inference (<100ms p50 for standard prompts), secure key ownership, region gating satisfied, and cost per token within your projected budget. for us: validate routing, model performance, and integration with your ops workflow.
[08:15] Liam O'Neal: Latency metric is a big one — can you run synthetic tests using our traces?
[08:20] Rohit Patel: yes if you share traces we can run a benchmark and give a latency distribution. that's one of the next steps.
[08:28] Tomás Rivera: two more detailed items: 1) TLS termination — can you support mTLS between our services and the endpoint? 2) can you integrate with our SSO for engineers accessing the console?
[08:38] Rohit Patel: mTLS supported. SSO via SAML is supported; RBAC can be mapped to your groups. we'll include an SSO integration guide.
[08:47] Maya Chen: i'm going to surface an architecture pattern - do you want us to propose both privatelink and transit gateway variants in the diagram?
[08:54] Liam O'Neal: yes show both. also put costs next to each so we can pick.
[08:59] Rohit Patel: will do — we'll add an egress cost estimate per TB for each pattern and also include a DNS and route map.
[09:08] Sara Nguyen: any legal or data-processing addendum considerations? we need DPAs, subprocessor lists etc.
[09:14] Maya Chen: yes we have DPAs and subprocessor disclosures. for Private we can also include contractual language about where data is processed and who can access it.
[09:22] Nisha Kapoor: in terms of model variant support — we plan to use a smaller quantized model for latency-critical paths and a larger one for batch re-ranks. any constraints?
[09:32] Rohit Patel: supported — we support quantized weights and model selection routing. if you want mixed precision or custom kernels we'll need to run a quick compatibility check.
[09:42] Liam O'Neal: does Redwood handle model versioning and rollbacks? we have a strict change control process.
[09:48] Rohit Patel: yes model lifecycle management is built into the control plane with version pins, canary rollouts, and automatic rollback on regression.
[09:56] Tomás Rivera: what about monitoring and alerts? we need SLOs and SLIs integrated with PagerDuty.
[10:02] Maya Chen: observability hooks are available; you can export metrics to CloudWatch/Datadog/Prometheus and we can push alerts to PagerDuty.
[10:10] Sara Nguyen: one more thing — pen test results. do you provide recent pentest reports?
[10:15] Evelyn Park: yes we'll include the latest pentest redacted report in the security pack.
[10:19] Liam O'Neal: great. can we discuss a hypothetical topology: our VPC in eu-west-1 peered via transit gateway to a Redwood node in eu-west-1 with Direct Connect from our onprem in ap-southeast-2. will an inference request from apac route to eu or do you recommend local apac nodes?
[10:36] Rohit Patel: in that topology, if you peer the regions, traffic can egress to eu nodes but that will add latency. better pattern: spin up regional apac nodes (ap-southeast-2) and pin the request routing to region to satisfy residency and lower latency. we can replicate model artifacts to the region using encrypted transfer.
[10:57] Nisha Kapoor: replication — is that synchronous? what about consistency and model versioning across regions?
[11:03] Rohit Patel: replication is asynchronous by default. model versions are coordinated via the control plane; we can enforce atomic version promotion across regions during rollout windows.
[11:13] Sara Nguyen: any bandwidth considerations for model sync? we have 100s of GBs for a few models.
[11:19] Rohit Patel: sync bandwidth depends on model size and frequency of updates. we recommend staged pushes and delta syncs for large models. we'll include a rough bandwidth estimate in our follow up.
[11:32] Liam O'Neal: how do you handle backups and snapshots of model artifacts?
[11:36] Rohit Patel: snapshots are stored encrypted and can be retention-controlled in your account if you own the storage. otherwise we store encrypted snapshots in Redwood-managed buckets and give you access or export.
[11:47] Maya Chen: switching gears — procurement and contract questions: do you have an enterprise procurement checklist?
[11:53] Evelyn Park: yes we have a procurement sheet and standard terms; for Private deployments we often negotiate an enterprise agreement outlining SLAs, support and onboarding credits.
[12:03] Nisha Kapoor: SLA specifics — what is your standard latency and uptime SLA for dedicated/private?
[12:09] Maya Chen: uptime SLAs are typically 99.9% for Dedicated and Private; latency SLOs are target-based and depend on model and capacity. we can negotiate tighter SLAs on enterprise contracts.
[12:20] Tomás Rivera: curious about autoscaling — can nodes scale based on queue depth or token throughput?
[12:26] Rohit Patel: yes autoscaling policies are flexible: by concurrent requests, queue depth, request rate, or token throughput. we also have burst capacity for short spikes.
[12:36] Sara Nguyen: are there any documented limitations around request sizes or sequence lengths that affect kernel selection?
[12:42] Rohit Patel: large sequence lengths can increase memory and latency; the runtime will choose different kernels and batching behavior. we'll provide guidance on optimal sequence lengths and batching profiles.
[12:55] Liam O'Neal: ok we're almost at the end — one last ask: for the pilot we're going to channel engineer time. can you estimate cost for a 4-week Dedicated pilot in eu-west-1 + ap-southeast-2 with moderate throughput?
[13:09] Maya Chen: we can spin a rough estimate — need your expected RPS and average tokens per request. once you share the spreadsheet we'll run the cost calc.
[13:18] Nisha Kapoor: we'll share numbers. also include a scenario with privatelink vs nodes-in-account.
[13:25] Rohit Patel: noted. we'll prepare both cost scenarios and latency tradeoffs.
[13:31] Sara Nguyen: anything else from your side?
[13:34] Maya Chen: not yet. i'm going to summarize the follow ups and action items.
[13:38] Maya Chen: recap: Redwood will send security pack (SOC2, pen test, KMS notes, SSO guide, network CIDRs), SE will prepare architecture sketches for privatelink and transit gateway with cost and egress estimates, AetherWave will share egress volumes/traces and required regions, target pilot week proposed in Q3, schedule deep technical planning call next week.
[13:58] Liam O'Neal: that sounds good. thanks everyone.
[14:01] Tomás Rivera: thanks.
[14:03] Nisha Kapoor: thanks all.
[14:05] Evelyn Park: we'll follow up via email with the attachments.
[14:08] Maya Chen: great talk soon. bye.
[14:10] [END OF CALL]

Note: transcription contains occasional mislabels and audio dropouts; full call audio will be attached in the CRM."
